implemented: Added detect_conflict_evidence(claim, evidence_items), a stdlib-only deterministic lexical conflict candidate detector.
Added numeric conflict detection for retrieved chunks that share the claim context/year/named marker or strong lexical overlap but contain different numeric markers instead of the claim number.
Added explicit-negation detection for required markers near conservative negation terms such as not, shall not, no, never, without, bu de, forbid/cancel/stop style Chinese terms.
verify_claim now returns conflict_evidence with has_conflicts, items, summary, and method=deterministic_lexical_v1.
When a claim would otherwise be supported but conflict candidates are present, verify_claim downgrades status to needs_verification and prepends conflict_evidence_detected to reasons.
Added unit tests for different-number conflict, negated-marker conflict, clean support with no conflict, and HTTP JSON presence of conflict_evidence.
Hardened tools/run_quality_gates.py so the py-compile gate uses a temporary PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX and does not depend on writable repository __pycache__ directories.
Updated README, ROADMAP, and retrieval evaluation docs to distinguish deterministic conflict candidates from full semantic/NLI conflict detection.
not_implemented: This is not semantic entailment and does not prove a real contradiction.
No LLM/NLI model, vector retrieval, embedding pipeline, reranker, or cross-sentence reasoning was added.
The detector intentionally produces audit candidates and forces human verification rather than automatically rejecting a claim as false.

risks: Numeric conflict detection can still flag unrelated numbers if retrieved chunks are lexically similar enough; therefore the output is named conflict_evidence candidates and only downgrades to needs_verification.
Negation detection is substring/window based and conservative; it may miss implicit contradictions or long-distance negation.
The py-compile gate now isolates pycache writes, but future direct py_compile commands outside the gate may still hit inherited __pycache__ ownership on this machine.
